newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05-0.10 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05-0.10 lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open 0.05 to 0.10 cent per lb lower on Monday, as dealers expected a continued correction after a recent rally to seven-month highs.

Friday, New York raws settled weaker in the nearby months, but off the lows as steady buying in the May/July spread limited losses. Spot May finished down 0.04 at 11.33 cents, having ranged from 11.34 and 11.23. The back months settled 0.01 lower to up 0.02.

After the close Friday, the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 8 showed non-commercial long positions increased by 5,127 lots, to 32,213, while non-commercial short positions increased by 2,233 lots, to 8,024 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 2,270 lots, to 71,319 lots and commercial short rose by 13,115 lots, to 118,790 lots.
Nonreportable long positions increased by 3,858 lots, to 51,303 lots, while nonreportable short positions decreased by 4,093 lots, to 28,021 lots.
LIFFE white sugar futures corrected lower early Monday, with May at $310.50 at 0905 EDT/1405 GMT, down $1.30.

On the physical side, Pakistan tendered to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal whites to arrive in Karachi by June and July, with 25,000 tonnes to arrive no later than June 20, 1997, and the remaining 25,000 tonnes by July 10.
Results are still awaited in Sri Lanka's tender to buy 12,500 tonnes of sugar for delivery in the first half of June. The tender closed on April 11.
